chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Hawkins as master of the tenor, with Caldwell and Prince Robinson
summary: Among early tenor players the three to get by were Hawk, Happy and Prince Robinson; Hawkins was master of slap tongue before dropping it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Well, I mean that's -- of course, you went -- I mean you must have been, well, I mean, for better players, (unintelligible) there wasn't anything but him when you really began, was there?
So you must have been almost -- well, I suppose you and Stump Evans there were the first to get it
That's true. That's true. Prince Robinson --
Well, Prince Robinson is -- would he be --
He's a bit later, isn't he?

Yeah, because (unintelligible) when they'd say tenor players, they'd say Hawk, here (unintelligible), it was Hawk, Happy and Big Prince Robinson. So them were the three you had to get by because Bean was the master. We all called Hawk the master. That's what he was.
When you first heard him with Mamie playing with Smith, I mean most of -- there was still quite a bit of slap tonguing.
He was the master of slap tongue, yes, he was.
Yeah. But, of course, he gradually realized it was corny --
